Position Summary
The Vice President, Strategic Account Management is a strategic commercial leader responsible for strengthening and growing high-value partnerships across A Place for Mom’s (APFM) network of senior living communities, REITs, and other national or regional channels. As the primary executive-level relationship owner for key senior living partners, the VP will drive revenue growth, move-in conversion, and network retention while delivering exceptional value to APFM’s providers and the families we serve.

The VP will focus on three priorities: strengthening the network through better provider performance, more complete community data, and strong retention; aligning account management activities with the provider behaviors that best serve families; and raising provider Net Promoter Score (NPS) by increasing the value providers see in APFM.

The ideal candidate is a proven…

sections.title:
Key Responsibilities
Network Strength, Retention & Revenue
bullets: Drive revenue growth and move-in conversion through account strategies for national and regional senior living providers, REITs, and channel partners.
Own retention of the existing provider network, identifying at-risk or underperforming communities early and intervening so families continue to have strong choices.
Own network health: monitor network size, coverage, and provider performance against family demand, and flag coverage gaps to the provider acquisition team.

sections.title: Provider Performance & Family Experience
bullets: Align provider behaviors with APFM’s service model to deliver better outcomes for families.
Partner with senior living operators to improve their performance on APFM referrals, from the first family conversation through tour and move-in.
Drive more complete, accurate, and current community information across the network so APFM can match each family with the right options.
Build a provider performance scorecard and account planning process that gives account managers and providers a shared view of performance and measurable improvement goals.

sections.title: Provider Value & Executive Relationships
bullets: Own provider NPS for the network: establish a consistent measurement cadence, diagnose what drives promoters and detractors, and lead the action plans that raise it.
Set and uphold a proactive communication standard for the account management team, including regular performance updates, timely responses, and clear advance notice of changes that affect providers.
Lead executive-level business reviews that demonstrate APFM’s value relative to each provider’s investment, connecting APFM referrals to move-ins, occupancy, and revenue.
Act as the voice of the provider within APFM, bringing feedback and insights to Product, Operations, Finance, and executive leadership, and reporting back to providers on what changed as a result.
Establish and maintain strong, influential relationships with senior living industry executives, serving as a trusted strategic partner and advisor.
Represent APFM at industry conferences and events to strengthen partnerships and elevate APFM’s market presence.

sections.title: Team Leadership & Collaboration
bullets: Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of account managers to consistently exceed revenue, conversion, provider performance, provider NPS, and network retention objectives.

Define the core competencies, activities, and performance expectations for the account management role, and connect them directly to the provider behaviors and network outcomes the team is accountable for.

Manage team performance against a balanced scorecard of revenue, provider performance, network retention, and provider NPS, and partner with Finance and People teams to align incentives with those outcomes.
Partner with Product, Data Science, Operations, Marketing, and Sales to improve the provider experience and measure the impact of account management work on provider outcomes.
Champion new processes, tools, and structures that improve account management effectiveness at scale.
Perform other duties as assigned.

ashby:agentio:50846fc1-7ff0-4f51-ac68-80.summary:
Agentio enables marketers to buy creator-led ads as easily and scalably as Meta or Google ads, automating sourcing, pricing, contracting, delivery, and measurement. Work that took months now happens in minutes.

We're on a mission to transform an $800B digital ad ecosystem by shifting ad spend into the hands of creators. That means better outcomes for marketers and creators finally being paid in proportion to the value they create. The shift is accelerating. Unilever's CEO has said the company will move roughly half its ad budget into social and creators, and Unilever spends around $9-10B annually. As those dollars move, they need performance-grade pipes. Agentio is how they flow to creators with the speed, control, and measurement marketers expect. Brands like Uber, DoorDash, and Bombas run creator campaigns on Agentio with the same rigor and accountability as their core performance…

sections.title: About Agentio
paras: Agentio has raised $56M at a $340M valuation, including a Series B led by Forerunner that followed our Series A within a calendar year. Backed by Benchmark, Craft, and AlleyCorp. Named to Forbes' Next Billion-Dollar Startups (2025) and Inc.'s Best Places to Work (2026).

sections.title: About the Role
paras: You'll own a book of accounts after the sale closes and be accountable for growing it through expansion, cross-platform adoption, deeper and more senior relationships, and net dollar retention. You carry a quota. Your job is to wake up every morning figuring out how to make your number bigger.

Your book will span our core accounts, growth-stage brands where the work is prioritization, finding expansion others would miss, and reactivating churned accounts. Increasingly, it will also include our key accounts. Our key account sales team is closing Fortune 500 brands and large enterprise organizations, and once they sign, someone has to grow them. That means navigating procurement, brand safety review, and approval chains that span many stakeholders, engaging senior brand leadership as a peer, and playing a long game where a single expansion can take quarters to land and be worth more than an entire core book. Direct enterprise experience is a real advantage here, but it isn't a requirement. What we need is the seniority and judgment to grow into that work quickly.

As a senior member of the team, you'll also help define how we grow accounts at Agentio. There is no settled playbook for this motion yet. You'll create narratives, test them, and share what works, and as the enterprise segment scales, you'll help write how we serve it.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own a revenue number. You're goaled on NDR against your book, with individual quota and individual accountability.

Sell after the sale. Identify expansion opportunities, build the case for increased budgets, drive adoption of new products and platforms as we launch them, and defend our share against incumbent agencies and channels competing for the same dollars.
Multi-thread and go top-down. Build relationships beyond your day-to-day contact, engage brand leadership to unstick problems, and know when and how to deploy our executives for top-to-top pressure.

Navigate large organizations to yes. As key accounts enter your book, work through procurement, legal, brand safety, and measurement review. Map the org, find the real decision-makers, sequence approvals across stakeholders, and keep momentum through processes designed to slow you down.

Convert measurement into investment. Our clients validate creator spend through MMM, lift studies, and platform attribution that don't always agree. You'll navigate those challenges and translate them into further investment.
Manage a full portfolio. Know where the growth is in your book, keep every account healthy, and catch drift before the client tells you.
Help author the playbook. Codify what works, thought-lead across the team, and shape how Agentio grows accounts as we scale.

sections.title: The bar:
bullets: 8+ years in advertising or media sales, account management, or client success, with demonstrated individual ownership of revenue outcomes. You have carried a quota throughout your career, you know what it was, and you know how you performed against it. Portfolio or team numbers don't substitute.

A career's worth of expansion wins you personally sourced and closed, at-risk accounts you saved and converted into better terms, and budget you won before the performance data existed to justify it. Specific accounts, specific figures, specific outcomes.

Executive presence. You have spent real time in rooms with senior brand leadership, you can walk in and own the conversation, and clients at that level treat you as a peer. You know how to pre-invest in senior relationships before you need them, and how to brief your own executives for top-to-top plays.

Autonomy and commercial instinct. You identify opportunity and risk in your book before anyone flags it, decide with incomplete information, and act without manager intervention. You bring your leadership outcomes and learnings rather than questions about what to do next.
Deep fluency in ad platforms and performance data.
Comfort operating without a safety net. We’re a start-up that wants to move fast, we want someone that has the confidence to identify opportunities and the conviction to act quickly.

ashby:anrok:a7b9b79d-c91b-436a-94f6-2c5d.summary:
Anrok is the leading AI-driven tax automation platform enabling businesses to expand globally without compliance complexity.

As the digital economy has grown 6x over the last decade, software businesses have gone from not worrying about sales tax to needing to monitor exposure, calculate rates, and file returns across 20+ US states and many countries worldwide. This creates a critical bottleneck for companies that should be able to transact with customers everywhere.

Anrok eliminates this complexity by connecting with billing and payment systems to automate tax monitoring, calculations, and filing end-to-end. Our unified platform handles the ever-changing maze of tax laws at municipal, state, and federal levels—so companies can focus on growth, not compliance.

sections.title: In this role, you will:
paras: This role is not partner account management, and it's not a support desk for partner tickets. It's a leverage function: you build the technical credibility and the reusable assets that let partners sell, integrate, and support Anrok without you in every conversation.
bullets: Build durable technical relationships with our integration partners — billing platforms, payment processors, ERPs, and the accounting and consulting firms that implement them. You'll be the named technical contact their teams actually call.

Run technical enablement for partners: solution deep-dives, architecture reviews, demo environments, sample code, and reference implementations, so partner teams can scope and position Anrok accurately on their own.
Drive best-in-class integrations by teaching partners what Anrok does well and where the real tax edge cases live. Push existing integrations from functional to excellent.

Design and land embedded partnerships, where a partner surfaces Anrok's tax capabilities natively inside their own product. You'll scope the technical shape of these, build the case internally with Product and Engineering, and see them through to launch.
Own the technical lifecycle of our prebuilt integrations — building and maintaining them where that's the right move, and partnering with Engineering to productionize the ones that need to scale.
Equip the Sales team to use the ecosystem: which partner to bring in, at what stage, for which technical problem. Build the internal enablement that makes this repeatable rather than tribal.
Source and evaluate new partner opportunities, including for lead generation. Build the business case for new connectors and integrations, and be honest about which ones aren't worth building.
Serve as the voice of the partner ecosystem to Product and Engineering, turning what you hear across dozens of partner conversations into high-signal roadmap input.

sections.title: What excites us:
bullets: 4+ years in Solutions Engineering, Partner Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or a similar partner- or customer-facing technical role.
Extensive hands-on experience with REST APIs, webhooks, and integration architecture. You can read a partner's API docs and tell them where the tax logic should live.
Experience working with technology partners, ISVs, or platform ecosystems — co-solutioning, joint architecture work, or technical enablement at scale.
You're as comfortable with a partner's VP of Engineering as you are with their sales team and our AEs.
You build things that outlast the conversation: documentation, demos, reference architectures, internal enablement. Strong written communication is a must.
You're comfortable owning a cross-functional initiative where you have to earn buy-in from leaders who don't report to you.
Familiarity with quote-to-cash, billing platforms (Stripe, Chargebee, Recurly, Zuora, NetSuite), or indirect tax is a strong plus. Deep curiosity about it is the requirement.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: As a Solutions Engineer, you will work directly with law firms to turn complex legal workflows into working AI solutions. You will embed with clients, understand their processes and technical environment, and own deployments from discovery and prototyping through integration, go-live, and adoption. This is a hands-on, client-facing role: you will run working sessions, build and test solutions, troubleshoot issues, and help people put AI to work. You should enjoy getting into the technical details as much as explaining what you’ve built to the people who will use it.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Embed with client organizations and run structured discovery across teams and practice groups, mapping workflows, systems, and data flows to identify where AI can have the greatest impact.
Work one-on-one with lawyers, paralegals, legal ops staff, and technical stakeholders to translate day-to-day pain points into clear requirements and practical solutions.
Build and test lightweight proofs-of-concept for document review, form filling, intake, drafting, redlining, and matter management, using APIs, scripts, and workflow automation tools where needed.
Configure AI workflows and connect them to client systems, working with technical teams on integrations, troubleshooting, and validation before rollout.
Run hands-on demos and training sessions that help users understand how the solutions work and adopt them in their daily practice.
Own the go-live from kickoff through adoption, coordinating technical resources on both sides and resolving issues as they arise.
Serve as a trusted technical point of contact for client stakeholders, running structured check-ins and business reviews to understand what’s working and what needs improvement.
Translate findings from deployments into actionable feedback for August’s engineering team, including reproducible issues, integration needs, and opportunities to improve the product.

sections.title: What we’re looking for
bullets: Strong technical problem-solving skills: you can break down an unfamiliar workflow, understand how its systems fit together, and build a practical solution.
Comfort writing lightweight scripts, working with APIs and structured data, and debugging integrations. Experience with Python or JavaScript is especially useful.
Strong product sense: you understand what makes a workflow painful and can translate that understanding into something people actually use.
Business acumen and clear communication: you can earn trust with a managing partner, a legal ops analyst, and a technical stakeholder, and explain complex ideas in straightforward terms.
Natural curiosity and comfort with ambiguity: you ask good questions, investigate beyond the obvious answer, and take ownership when there is no established playbook.

1–3 years of experience in solutions engineering, implementation engineering, technical consulting, software engineering, or a similarly hands-on technical role. Experience working directly with customers is valuable; a background in law or legal services is a plus.
Familiarity with AI tools, LLM-powered applications, or workflow automation platforms such as Zapier, Make, or n8n is helpful.
Excitement about working in person at our NYC office with a team that values precision, pace, and constant reinvention.

ashby:darkroom:4f43c38c-7559-499e-9e67-f.summary:

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow , a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

sections.title: About Darkroom
paras: Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos) . Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

sections.title: About the role
paras: We are looking for a deeply technical Senior Retention Specialist to own the CRM build for a high-growth consumer technology client. You will architect and implement the flows and automations that carry the program, own the segmentation logic behind them, and hold the channel KPIs that determine whether any of it lands in the inbox.

You are standing this program up from the ground, not inheriting it. The list starts near 20,000 and scales rapidly behind a significant acquisition investment — which puts real pressure on deliverability, list hygiene, and data hygiene from day one. Volume ramps to 40–60 emails a month, and increasingly granular segmentation is what generates that output. Automation is the core of the program: lead capture, welcome series, and the first-conversion funnel first, then subscription activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back. You will work in an enterprise-grade platform — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, Customer.io , or comparable.
You are the person who knows the platform better than anyone else on the team. When something does not fire, does not render, or does not deliver, you find out why.

sections.title: A day in the life
bullets: Build and QA the flows, automations, and campaigns that run your client's program — from lead capture and welcome through activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back.
Implement the segmentation and audience logic behind the calendar, and build the dynamic content that makes personalization work at volume.
Own the technical setup and health of the client's ESP instance: integrations, data feeds, event tracking, templates, and modules.
Monitor and own channel performance and deliverability, escalating and fixing issues before they affect the program.
Troubleshoot anything that misfires — a flow that does not trigger, a segment that under-populates, a template that breaks in Outlook — and document the fix.
QA every build end to end before launch: logic, rendering, links, personalization, suppression.
Design and run the testing roadmap with your Associate Director, and report results honestly.
Partner with the Copy & Content Specialist to get copy and creative into the build accurately and on schedule.

sections.title: What It's Like to Work at Darkroom
paras: Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

ashby:january:f13df887-838e-4324-834b-9f.summary:
Collections today works like an emergency room. The doctors carry too many patients, everyone arrives at their worst moment, and nobody has their chart. We're making it primary care. January personalizes interactions and optimizes decisions across every stage of consumer credit. We started in the hardest, most broken stage, because if it works there it works anywhere.

Most consumers want to pay what they owe. They want a way out, not a break. We've serviced over $20 billion in debt across more than 20 million consumers. We see more people with charged-off loans each year than all but the top five US banks. Those consumers rate us about 50% higher than the banks that lent them the money. Creditors net over 30% more because we collect more and charge less.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: As a Product Manager, you'll own one of our highest-leverage surfaces: how we reach consumers, how we talk with them and how we earn the trust that turns a missed payment into a fresh start. The work decides whether someone in their hardest financial moment gets a robocall or a way out.

We're hiring product managers for two teams. We'll figure out the right fit with you. You'll report to our Director of Product. We see these roles as some of the most important we'll fill as we scale from a single product into a multi-product company. We're widening the aperture. Collections gave us one planet. The rest of the solar system comes next.

One team owns the LLM infrastructure behind every consumer conversation: chatbot, voice, email and text. You'll push it toward a borrower experience that adapts to each person in real time, further than the industry thinks possible. The other owns the systems that send millions of communications an hour, email, SMS and letters, plus the experimentation engine behind them. You'll build toward outbound that tunes itself, learning what to say and when without a human in the loop.

sections.title: What We Need
bullets: You treat prescription before diagnosis as a sin. You never stop at symptoms. You decompose to root causes fast.
You decide with incomplete information. You find the few things that matter most and go get them quickly.
You bring principles for what to do now and what to do later. You don't try to do everything at once.
You hold an absurdly high bar. You know a couple of points is the difference between an average product and an exceptional one.
You care more about making the best decision than about being right. You update fast when the evidence changes.
You reason from data and design experiments that isolate cause. You go deep enough with engineers to argue about the system, not just the roadmap.
You already push LLM tooling deep into your own work and want to go further than anyone has let you. You'll build the skills and workflows the rest of the company runs on.
You've owned a product strategy end to end and it moved something real.

sections.title: How We Work
paras: As a New York City-based company, we are dedicated to transparent, fair, and equitable compensation practices that reflect our commitment to fostering an environment where all team members are valued and supported. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.
bullets: Decentralization beats control. The best calls get made by the people closest to them, not routed up a chain. You'll set the standards that let the team decide without you in the room.
Speed beats perfection. You run tight loops, act at 70% on reversible calls and adjust as you learn. Fast loops beat slow ones.
Candor beats comfort. You'd rather hear a hard truth early than a polite sidestep that wastes everyone's time.
Writing beats the average meeting . Clarity scales.

We operate at every altitude. No one here lives only on Mount Olympus, not even the leaders. We get into the trenches to learn the ground truth. We constantly refine our information flows so that our decisions are driven by the best, most up to date inputs.

We build in person, at least three days a week in our office in Nolita , with a growing group coming in every day. Random run-ins cross-pollinate ideas. Face time builds trust no thread can. Building alongside people makes work far more fun.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: You'll own the core design and generation experience — the heart of the product, where a designer goes from an idea to something they'd actually put in front of their director. This is the wedge the whole company is built on, and you'll have ownership over it. We're looking for someone who goes deep on that core and can flex outward when the company needs it — not a generalist who floats across everything at the surface. Your north star in the first months: get a skeptical, non-technical fashion designer to a genuine "this is magic" moment in their very first session, and then again and again.

Generative products aren't like normal software. You're not writing a spec for one exact output — you're designing for a range of outputs you don't fully control, for users who shouldn't have to understand what's happening under the hood. You'll own the core generation and design workflow end to end, obsessing over activation and turning a doubtful creative into a believer in their first session. You'll define what "good output" means for our users and build the evaluation habits to know whether the product is actually getting better, design for trust so non-technical users know when to lean on the model and variability feels graceful instead of broken, and hold both sides of the enterprise equation — the everyday creative and the director who signs the contract — when their needs pull apart. You'll run tight discovery — user interviews, competitive teardowns, heavy dogfooding, often all in the same week — and turn those insights into shipped launches fast.

sections.title: Who you are
paras: We're serious about hiring for trajectory over pedigree. If you don't check every box but you're clearly wired for this, apply anyway.
bullets: Extremely high ownership. You figure out what needs to happen, unblock yourself, and do it. Bad conditions — thin resources, missing data, a hostile stakeholder — are problems you route around or reverse, not reasons it didn't get done.

You have an eye. You can look at several generated design concepts and articulate why some are off and one is sellable. Product sense, for our users, is aesthetic sense plus workflow empathy — and you have both, or are hungry to sharpen them.
A systems thinker. You see the whole ecosystem a feature touches and instinctively flag the thing everyone assumes someone else owns.
A first-principles thinker. You reason from the job-to-be-done and the nature of the medium, and you're willing to throw out a standard AI-product pattern when it doesn't serve our users.

Fluent in — or a fast learner of — probabilistic systems. You think in distributions and evals, not single specs. We care more about how quickly you get this than how many years you've formally done it.
Resilient and creative under real constraints — which is most of the job at an early-stage startup.
AI-native in how you work. Comfortable using ChatGPT, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Town, or other AI prototyping and productivity tools to accelerate research, prototyping, and execution.
Data-driven. You define clear product metrics, use quantitative and qualitative evidence to make decisions, and are comfortable in Amplitude.

Customer obsession: Everything we build starts with the customer. We listen deeply, move quickly, and obsess over delivering tools that make their work faster and more creative.

paras: Do you love product problems where real money moves, mistakes have consequences, and a better workflow is worth millions in time and trust? Are you a self-starter who thrives on technical depth, systems thinking, and genuine customer stakes? Then this role is for you.

We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own Vendor Spend: the vendor-payment layer of Wrapbook. This role owns how production companies pay their vendors — every payment method, the workflows around each payment, and the tracking and reporting that show customers exactly what's been paid. Your mandate is to broaden and speed up how vendors get paid, push toward straight-through processing, and open up net-new ways for productions to spend — while keeping every dollar accurate, compliant, and fraud-resistant.

This is one of the higher-leverage roles in the product org. Vendor payments touch cash flow, fraud and AML exposure, tax reporting, and the general ledger, and they sit at the crossroads of banking, accounting, and go-to-market. You'll own a domain with high technical complexity, a large cross-team surface area, and a direct line to customer and business outcomes.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Own the roadmap and vision for Vendor Spend — aligning customer needs and business priorities into a clear, sequenced plan you can defend, and defining the success metrics that prove it's working (adoption, cost and fraud reduction, revenue signals).

Expand and streamline how productions pay AP vendors — ACH (moving toward faster settlement), checks, direct-to-bank processing, card payments, and international — reducing time-to-payment and pushing toward true straight-through processing.

Lead the expense-management bet , a meaningful 0→1 opportunity: Wrapbook-issued spend/purchasing cards and virtual AP cards for invoice payments, including issuance, controls, and how card spend flows back into accounting.

Advocate for accuracy, compliance, and fraud protection. Positive pay and check-fraud prevention, ACH transaction screening and AML controls, and vendor tax reporting (1099) are core to the domain, not afterthoughts.
Partner with our banking infrastructure team on payment rails , defining clear service boundaries so vendor-payment workflows and the underlying bank transport evolve independently without surprises.
Keep vendor payments correct in the ledger , partnering with Accounting so payments and their reconciliation flow cleanly into production accounting.

Triage and prioritize competing demands from across the company — other product teams, Client Operations, Sales, Finance, Risk, Legal, and Support all touch this domain — managing them as part of your roadmap rather than as interruptions.
Use AI tools daily to accelerate your workflow — from discovery and analysis to writing, code comprehension, and prototyping. We expect our PMs to be builders, not just strategists.

bullets: 5+ years of product management experience in a SaaS, fintech, or similarly complex technical environment.

A track record of measurable outcomes, not just shipped features. You can point to products you drove that moved a real number — adoption, new market or segment access, cost or fraud reduction, revenue — and explain your specific contribution.

Domain proximity to money movement. Background in accounts payable, vendor/B2B payments, card issuance, or accounting is strongly preferred, so you can go deep quickly rather than ramping from zero on how funds and ledgers actually work.
A technical orientation. You reason with engineering about systems, data models, integrations, fund flows, and failure modes without heavy hand-holding.

Active, daily AI usage in your PM workflow — not experimental and not just ChatGPT. You use LLMs, AI-assisted coding tools, and AI workflows as core parts of how you ship, and can articulate specifically how AI has changed your PM work and where it's headed.
Experience owning products with high cross-functional surface area , where other teams and stakeholders depend on the systems and workflows you own.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a bias toward action, balanced against the compliance and quality bar a payments product demands.
Comfort with ambiguity — able to dive deep and become a subject-matter expert in an unfamiliar, technically complex domain.

sections.title: About the role

sections.title: About the role
paras: As Claude reaches more people, including individuals, businesses, developers building on our APIs, and the platforms and resellers building on top of those, knowing who is on the other side of a request and what they are allowed to do becomes foundational to running our products responsibly. Creating a centralized identity, verification, and access system that every Claude surface draws on is important to accomplishing our mission.

We are hiring a Product Manager to own the safe access. The primitives are the building blocks the rest of Anthropic uses to manage access to models and capabilities: access programs, accounts, organization linking, verifications, user APIs for platforms, and the internal tooling teams use. You will own the end-to-end product experience and strategy for internal and external access,, across every surface.

This is a role for a strong executor with the ability to be agile in shipping in a 0-1 product space. Safe access is a new product that sits on the critical path of every model launch and every access program. Requirements arrive from many organizations at once, and most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it.

sections.title: Key responsibilities
bullets: Own the product strategy and roadmap for the account and access primitives, with the goal that any team at Anthropic can provision access or run an access program with minimal support. This is highly ambiguous and requires a lot of cross team coordination and deep understanding of the systems of today.

Own the end-to-end experience of getting and managing access for internal stakeholders (research, model launches, safeguards, go-to-market) and for external customers and partners, and keep it consistent across every surface. This requires thinking through many user types, with vastly different experiences.

Support the API designs and the UX of the access APIs that platforms, resellers, and internal services integrate with. Work through the designs with engineering and make calls on the primitives yourself.
Partner with the trusted access and verification product managers so that new programs compose from shared primitives rather than one-off builds.
Coordinate across the product, safeguards, legal, and go-to-market teams, and drive alignment when their requirements conflict.

greenhouse:eleoshealth:4947873101.summary:
The people who deliver care in our communities and homes do some of the most important work in healthcare. But too often, theyʼre asked to spend their time navigating paperwork, administrative burden, and problems they only discover after something has already gone wrong.

Weʼre building the system of action for community-based care - helping behavioral health, hospice, home health, and other care teams spend less time reacting to problems and more time focused on the people they serve.

Powered by our Polaris AI, Eleos works alongside clinicians and their teams to understand whatʼs happening across care in real time and take action before issues become problems, reducing administrative burden, protecting revenue and compliance, and giving care teams more time and capacity to deliver great care.

sections.title: Who is Eleos Health?
paras: Our vision is a world where care teams can stay one step ahead, rather than constantly catching up. Weʼre helping shift an entire industry from reactive to proactive, and we need talented people to help us get there.

You'll be the HH&H compliance subject matter expert across the company — the bridge between our customers' clinical realities and our product, engineering, sales, and implementation teams. You'll translate regulatory frameworks like CMS Conditions of Participation, OASIS-E, HOPE, PDGM, and hospice eligibility standards into actionable product requirements, compliance rulesets, and customer-facing guidance, while helping build the compliance dashboard and custom rules engine for the Care at Home vertical.

sections.title: Who are you?
paras: You are someone who has lived the frustration of manual, fragmented compliance in home health and hospice and wants to build the technology that actually fixes it. You've spent real time delivering direct patient care and have since moved into quality assurance or compliance leadership, so you know both sides of the equation — what clinicians live day to day and what auditors expect on paper. You're comfortable in ambiguity and energized by cross-functional work, moving fluidly between product conversations, customer discovery calls, and frontline clinical detail. You're confident enough in your regulatory knowledge to push back when something isn't right, and you find genuine satisfaction in turning dense CMS language into something an engineer or a salesperson can actually use.

sections.title: How will you contribute?
bullets: Provide clinical validation and subject matter expertise for AI-driven compliance prompts, Live Quality Assist nudges, and compliance dashboard checks, reviewing AI-generated narrative notes, OASIS responses, and HOPE items for clinical accuracy and regulatory alignment.

Lead discovery sessions with HH&H executives, QA/QAPI directors, and clinicians to identify compliance needs and workflow gaps, and support compliance implementations end-to-end — including data schema validation, EHR ingestion review, and custom rules development.
Serve as the HH&H compliance SME during customer meetings, QBRs, and onsite visits alongside sales, customer success, and implementation teams.

Educate internal teams on HH&H compliance personas, regulatory frameworks, and market dynamics, and partner with Product, Clinical Strategy, Engineering, and Sales Engineering to keep HH&H needs reflected in product and go-to-market materials.
Monitor changes in CMS regulations, MAC and payer requirements, and accreditation standards, translating market and competitive signals into product and positioning recommendations.

greenhouse:endorlabs:4741319005.summary:
AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and…

This is a high-impact role for a seasoned product manager who understands that large enterprises do not simply need faster database deployments — they need governed, secure, compliant, and measurable change delivery at scale.

The ideal candidate has a proven track record of bringing enterprise software products to market, strong execution discipline, and deep empathy for Fortune 500 and regulated enterprise customers operating in complex DevOps, data platform, security, and compliance environments.

sections.title: Who You Are
paras: You are a seasoned product manager who has successfully brought enterprise software products to market. You are comfortable with ambiguity but disciplined in execution. You can go deep with technical teams, speak credibly with enterprise customers, and communicate clearly with executives.

You understand that large enterprises do not just need faster delivery — they need safer, governed, compliant, and auditable delivery. You are excited about helping Liquibase become the standard for Database Change Governance in the AI era.

sections.title: What You’ll Own
paras: You will help define and advance Liquibase’s leadership position in Database Change Governance by shaping capabilities that make Liquibase the enterprise standard for governing database change across applications, environments, teams, pipelines, and data platforms.

Policy enforcement across development, test, staging, and production
Visibility across applications, teams, environments, and deployment pipelines
Audit-ready evidence for database change activity
Risk-based controls for database deployments
Governance of both human-generated and AI-generated database changes

greenhouse:phaidra:4719607005.summary:
Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation.

The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades.

Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically:

sections.title: About Phaidra
paras: Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. From achieving superhuman performance with DeepMind's AlphaGo , to reducing the energy required to cool Google's Data Centers by 40%, we deeply understand AI and how to apply it in production for massive impact.

Phaidra’s ability to achieve its mission is determined by our ability to work together — as defined by our core values: Agency, Velocity , Craft , and Truth . We seek individuals who embody these values, as they are instrumental in ensuring our team consistently delivers excellence and fosters an engaging and supportive culture

Phaidra is based in the USA, but we are 100% remote with no physical office. We hire employees internationally with the help of our partner, OysterHR . Our team is currently located throughout the USA, Canada, UK, Sweden, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Singapore, Australia, and India.
bullets: We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions.
We focus on industrial applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs — perfect for reinforcement learning.
We enable domain experts (our users) to configure the AI control systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them.

At RelationalAI , we’re solving one of the most important challenges in artificial intelligence: how to teach large language models the logic, semantics, and business context of the modern enterprise.

Frontier models are trained almost entirely on public data — they can speak about the world, but they don’t understand your business. We fix that.

RelationalAI has pioneered a breakthrough called Superalignment — technology that enables LLMs to learn natively from private, structured enterprise data inside the data cloud.

By combining this with relational knowledge graphs and our proprietary neuro/symbolic-relational reasoners , we deliver trustworthy decision intelligence : systems that use semantic models to truly understand how a business operates and can reason across its data to drive better outcomes.

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: We’re a globally distributed team of engineers, scientists, and builders redefining how AI learns from data. We believe that high-stakes decisions deserve frontier intelligence — intelligence that’s explainable, aligned, and grounded in reality.
If you’re driven by curiosity, thrive in complexity, and want to help build the system that brings true understanding to enterprise AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

sections.title: The Role
paras: You will be embedded inside our customers' hardest problems, and you will own the outcome until it works in production.

You'll sit with executives, domain experts, and data teams to find the decisions that actually move their business - inventory that's in the wrong place, risk concentrations nobody can see, fraud patterns that only emerge across three systems, capacity plans built on guesses. Then you'll model their world in our ontology, formulate the reasoning problem, write the PyRel, and ship something that runs against their real data in their own Snowflake account.

sections.title: Every engagement here produces two deliverables.
paras: The first is the one the customer sees: a working decision system that changes how they operate.

The second is the one that matters most to us: the pile of things you had to invent because our platform didn't have them yet. The modelling pattern you hand-rolled. The constraint formulation that should have been a primitive. The three-hour workaround where an API should have existed. You bring those back, you argue for them, and the strongest of them become product.
That second deliverable is why this role exists. If you only ever deliver the first one, we've hired a consultant. We're not hiring consultants.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own outcomes end to end - discovery, modelling, implementation, performance tuning, production hardening, and the measurement that proves it worked. Not a handoff at each stage. Yours.

Build, not describe - design and ship decision solutions on our modelling, reasoning, and learning stack: ontologies over customer data, rules, graph analytics, optimisation formulations, predictive models

Fill the gaps yourself - when a customer workflow is blocked on something the platform doesn't do, scope it and build it. Then push the general version upstream: read our source, form a hypothesis before you escalate, open the PR.

Close the loop with Product - every deployment generates a signal. Bring back reproductions, patterns, and specific failure modes ("the only way I could express this was by abusing X in this way"), not vibes. You are one of the loudest inputs into our roadmap.
Run technical discovery that gets to the truth - workshops, demos, and proofs of concept designed to find out whether we can actually solve the problem, not to look impressive.

Leave things better than you found them - document as you go, in the repo, same week. Turn one-off work into reusable reference implementations so the next person starts where you finished. No branch of yours should be diverging for a month.
Refuse shortcuts that compound - no undocumented config drift, no "it works now" without knowing why it broke, no restarting the service before you've captured the evidence.

sections.title: About the role:
paras: Remix is Via's premier transit planning and scheduling platform, trusted by transit agencies worldwide to design networks, model scenarios, and optimize service. We're looking for a Director of Product to define and drive the next era of Remix: a multimodal planning and scheduling system that gives transit agencies a single, authoritative place to make smarter decisions across every service type they operate.

This is a high-impact, high-ownership role. You will shape the vision for how agencies move from static schedules to data-driven, dynamically optimized operations — balancing labor union rules and contractual constraints with the operational agility modern transit demands. You will own the end-to-end product experience from strategic planning through live execution, and your work will directly affect how millions of riders experience public transit every day.

Build the framework for data-driven scheduling — enabling agencies to make optimal use of driver and vehicle time through intelligent analysis of ridership patterns, operational constraints, and service goals

Deeply understand and incorporate labor union rules, collective bargaining agreements, and workforce regulations into the product in a way that is structured yet flexible enough to adapt as those rules evolve
Connect planning and scheduling seamlessly to live operations, reducing the gap between what is scheduled and what is executed — improving accuracy, dispatcher confidence, and rider reliability
Partner closely with engineering, design, data science, and GTM teams to move from vision to shipped product with clear milestones and measurable outcomes
Engage directly and frequently with transit planners, schedulers, and operations leaders to surface unmet needs and validate product direction
Stay current on industry trends, emerging regulations, and competitive dynamics to keep Remix ahead of the market

bullets: You have 10+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex enterprise software products

Are a systems thinker who can hold both strategic vision and operational detail — you know when to zoom out and when to get into the weeds
Have strong instincts for simplifying complexity: translating divergent customer needs and intricate business rules into clean, scalable product decisions
Bring deep empathy for the professionals who use your product daily — planners, schedulers, dispatchers — and design with their real working context in mind

Can quickly become technically fluent in the underlying data models and entities that power scheduling and operations systems — blocks, runs, trips, stops, vehicles, duties, pairings — and can engage at that level of specificity with engineers and architects
